/-!
# Conjecture 10.59

by A. I. Sozutov

Is a $p'$-group $G$ locally nilpotent if it admits a splitting automorphism $\varphi$ of
prime order $p$ such that all subgroups of the form
$\langle g, g^{\varphi}, \ldots, g^{\varphi^{p-1}} \rangle$ are nilpotent?

An automorphism $\varphi$ of order $p$ is called *splitting* if
$g g^{\varphi} g^{\varphi^2} \cdots g^{\varphi^{p-1}} = 1$ for all $g \in G$.

Here $g^{\varphi}$ denotes the image $\varphi(g)$ of $g$ under $\varphi$. The group $G$ may be
infinite, and a $p'$-group is a group with no element of order $p$. A group is locally nilpotent
if all of its finitely generated subgroups are nilpotent.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

def IsLocallyNilpotent (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Group.IsNilpotent H

def IsSplittingAutomorphism (p : ℕ) (φ : MulAut G) : Prop :=
  orderOf φ = p ∧ ∀ g : G, ((List.range p).map fun i => (φ ^ i) g).prod = 1

$\varphi$ has order exactly $p$ and $g \varphi(g) \varphi^2(g) \cdots \varphi^{p-1}(g) = 1$

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib/GroupTheory/FixedPointFree.lean (fixed-point-free automorphisms; a different notion), MulAut, orderOf
justification.name: Kourovka.«10.59».IsSplittingAutomorphism

blocks.name: IsSplittingAutomorphism
blocks.text:
/-- An automorphism $\varphi$ of a group $G$ is a *splitting automorphism of order $p$* if
$\varphi$ has order exactly $p$ and $g \varphi(g) \varphi^2(g) \cdots \varphi^{p-1}(g) = 1$
for all $g \in G$. -/
def IsSplittingAutomorphism (p : ℕ) (φ : MulAut G) : Prop :=
  orderOf φ = p ∧ ∀ g : G, ((List.range p).map fun i => (φ ^ i) g).prod = 1

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isSplittingAutomorphism_inv_zmod_three :
    IsSplittingAutomorphism 2 (MulEquiv.inv (Multiplicative (ZMod 3))) := by
  refine ⟨?_, fun g => by simp [List.range_succ]⟩
  haveI : Fact (Nat.Prime 2) := ⟨Nat.prime_two⟩
  refine orderOf_eq_prime (by ext g; simp [pow_two]) fun h => ?_
  have := congrArg (fun ψ : MulAut (Multiplicative (ZMod 3)) => ψ (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1)) h
  simp at this
  exact absurd (congrArg Multiplicative.toAdd this) (by decide)
blocks.docstring: Inversion is a splitting automorphism of order $2$ of the cyclic group of order $3$.

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question (answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ p prime, ∀ G a p'-group, ∀ φ ∈ Aut G of order p with g·g^φ···g^{φ^{p-1}} = 1 for all g, (∀ g, ⟨g, g^φ, …, g^{φ^{p-1}}⟩ nilpotent) → G locally nilpotent); subtleties: G may be infinite so 'p'-group' must be fixed as 'no element of order p' (the notebook's usual convention, as opposed to 'periodic with all orders coprime to p'), 'nilpotent' for each φ-orbit subgroup is with class unbounded in g, φ has order exactly p (not merely φ^p = 1), and the trailing sentence 'An automorphism φ of order p is called splitting if …' is only the definition of splitting, not a further question.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same faithful content (p'-group as 'no element of order p', orderOf φ = p, ordered List.prod splitting identity, closure of {φ^i g : i < p} nilpotent for each g, local nilpotency as every FG subgroup nilpotent, G : Type). I verified (φ ^ i) g = φ^[i] g so the Nat.iterate encodings (c01/c05/c08) and the MulAut-power encodings agree, and that c05/c06's 'closure of each finite set' is equivalent to Subgroup.FG. c07 was chosen for readability: documented bespoke definitions (IsLocallyNilpotent, IsSplittingAutomorphism, orbitSubgroup) with an API lemma and a non-trivial test (inversion on ℤ/3 is a splitting automorphism of order 2), following the 1_40.lean precedent of defining generic notions in the problem file; it compiles with only the sorry warning. Used verbatim.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.59

by A. I. Sozutov

Is a $p'$-group $G$ locally nilpotent if it admits a splitting automorphism $\varphi$ of
prime order $p$ such that all subgroups of the form
$\langle g, g^{\varphi}, \ldots, g^{\varphi^{p-1}} \rangle$ are nilpotent?

An automorphism $\varphi$ of order $p$ is called *splitting* if
$g g^{\varphi} g^{\varphi^2} \cdots g^{\varphi^{p-1}} = 1$ for all $g \in G$.

Here $g^{\varphi}$ denotes the image $\varphi(g)$ of $g$ under $\varphi$. The group $G$ may be
infinite, and a $p'$-group is a group with no element of order $p$. A group is locally nilpotent
if all of its finitely generated subgroups are nilpotent.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.59»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- A group is *locally nilpotent* if every finitely generated subgroup is nilpotent. -/
def IsLocallyNilpotent (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Group.IsNilpotent H

/-- A nilpotent group is locally nilpotent. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyNilpotent.of_isNilpotent [Group.IsNilpotent G] : IsLocallyNilpotent G :=
  fun H _ => H.isNilpotent

/-- An automorphism $\varphi$ of a group $G$ is a *splitting automorphism of order $p$* if
$\varphi$ has order exactly $p$ and $g \varphi(g) \varphi^2(g) \cdots \varphi^{p-1}(g) = 1$
for all $g \in G$. -/
def IsSplittingAutomorphism (p : ℕ) (φ : MulAut G) : Prop :=
  orderOf φ = p ∧ ∀ g : G, ((List.range p).map fun i => (φ ^ i) g).prod = 1

/-- Inversion is a splitting automorphism of order $2$ of the cyclic group of order $3$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isSplittingAutomorphism_inv_zmod_three :
    IsSplittingAutomorphism 2 (MulEquiv.inv (Multiplicative (ZMod 3))) := by
  refine ⟨?_, fun g => by simp [List.range_succ]⟩
  haveI : Fact (Nat.Prime 2) := ⟨Nat.prime_two⟩
  refine orderOf_eq_prime (by ext g; simp [pow_two]) fun h => ?_
  have := congrArg (fun ψ : MulAut (Multiplicative (ZMod 3)) => ψ (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1)) h
  simp at this
  exact absurd (congrArg Multiplicative.toAdd this) (by decide)

/-- The subgroup $\langle g, g^{\varphi}, \ldots, g^{\varphi^{p-1}} \rangle$ of $G$ generated by
the images of $g$ under $\varphi^0, \varphi^1, \ldots, \varphi^{p-1}$. -/
def orbitSubgroup (p : ℕ) (φ : MulAut G) (g : G) : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.closure (Set.range fun i : Fin p => (φ ^ (i : ℕ)) g)

/--
Let $p$ be a prime and let $G$ be a $p'$-group, that is, a group with no element of order $p$.
Suppose that $G$ admits a splitting automorphism $\varphi$ of order $p$, i.e. an automorphism of
order exactly $p$ with $g g^{\varphi} g^{\varphi^2} \cdots g^{\varphi^{p-1}} = 1$ for all
$g \in G$, such that for every $g \in G$ the subgroup
$\langle g, g^{\varphi}, \ldots, g^{\varphi^{p-1}} \rangle$ is nilpotent. Is $G$ then locally
nilpotent?

The nilpotency class of $\langle g, g^{\varphi}, \ldots, g^{\varphi^{p-1}} \rangle$ may depend
on $g$; no uniform bound is assumed.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.59» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (p : ℕ) (G : Type) [Group G] (φ : MulAut G),
      p.Prime → (∀ g : G, orderOf g ≠ p) → IsSplittingAutomorphism p φ →
      (∀ g : G, Group.IsNilpotent (orbitSubgroup p φ g)) →
      IsLocallyNilpotent G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.59»

items: p'-group is formalized as 'no element of order p' (∀ g : G, orderOf g ≠ p), per the decomposition table, rather than 'periodic with all element orders coprime to p'. Infinite-order elements (orderOf g = 0) are permitted; elements of order p^k are implicitly excluded since they give an element of order p.

g^φ is read as φ(g) and the splitting product is the ordered product g · φ(g) · φ²(g) ··· φ^{p-1}(g) via List.prod over List.range p (Finset.prod is unavailable in noncommutative groups). The alternative convention g^φ = φ⁻¹(g) yields an equivalent condition and the same generated subgroups.
'Automorphism of prime order p' is formalized as orderOf φ = p (order exactly p), not φ ^ p = 1.
The nilpotency hypothesis on ⟨g, g^φ, …, g^{φ^{p-1}}⟩ is Group.IsNilpotent of the coerced subgroup for each g separately; no uniform bound on the nilpotency class is imposed.
G is quantified over Type (not Type*), following the convention in Kourovka/1_40.lean.

Two auxiliary declarations with proofs are included as basic API/tests for the bespoke definitions: a nilpotent group is locally nilpotent, and inversion on Multiplicative (ZMod 3) is a splitting automorphism of order 2.

reviewer_notes: Only real ambiguity: 'p'-group' for a possibly infinite group. Shipped reading is 'no element of order p' (no periodicity assumed), as fixed by the decomposition table and used by every candidate; the docstrings state this explicitly. Under the alternative 'periodic with orders coprime to p' reading the hypothesis would be stronger, so the universal statement would be weaker. Also noted: 'admits φ' (∃) is encoded as ∀ φ with the hypotheses as premises, which is equivalent since the conclusion does not mention φ. Non-vacuity checked: ℤ/3 with inversion and p = 2 satisfies all hypotheses. No candidate omitted the slot; no omission reasons to weigh.
